_readme: Every CSS selector the upload automation uses lives in this file, so the
portal's markup can change without anyone editing Python.
Each entry is a LIST of candidate selectors tried in order; the first one
that matches (and is visible, where visibility is required) wins. That
makes the automation tolerant of small markup differences and lets you
add the portal's real selector to the front of a list without deleting
the existing fallbacks.
The defaults below are best-effort guesses based on the portal being an
ASP.NET MVC app - they have NOT been verified against the live site.
Run 'python tools/inspect_page.py' to print the real selectors, then put
them at the front of the relevant lists.
Besides standard CSS, Playwright's :has-text('...') pseudo-class is
supported for matching an element by its visible text, and :text-is('...')
for an exact match.
Selectors under 'upload_dialog' are resolved INSIDE the dialog, not against
the whole page. The automation locates the dialog by finding the file input
and walking up to its enclosing dialog container, so these selectors can be
simple. That scoping matters: the Manage Application table behind the dialog
has its own SIP Batch filter listing every historical batch, and a
page-wide 'select[name*=Batch]' matches that filter instead of the dialog's
dropdown - which looks like success while the dialog stays empty.
Note on 'upload_dialog.upload_button': it must point at the button that
SUBMITS the dialog. On this portal that button is labelled 'Save', which is
why the Save candidates come first; 'Upload' is kept as a fallback. It must
NOT match the 'Upload New Applications' button that opens the dialog, nor
the dialog's own Close/Cancel button - the automation refuses both rather
than silently reopening or dismissing the dialog.
